text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE
- Exiled king Leka I is visiting the rebel-held town of Vlore in a bid to gain support for monarchy.
- There is no doubt President Sali Berisha is plotting against Prime Minister Bashkim Fino's national reconciliation government, Democratic Alliance Party leader Neritan Ceka said in interview.
- Editorial says some Democratic Party's MPs including Berisha's loyal adviser Genc Pollo do not t dare to visit south Albania even though they were elected there.
- Deputy Interior Minister and police chief Agim Shehu asked the Constitutional Court to rule on whether the government decision to sack him is against the constitution.
- VEFA holding company claims violence and lawlessness which hit the country last month caused it $302 million in losses, saying its mills, factories and supermarkets were looted and ruined.
- The paper accuses state-run television of being biased, saying it has remained in Berisha's hands even after the formation of a broad-based government.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- Two people died and 14 seriously injured after eating biscuits that apparently contained traces of a drug.
- A group of Democratic Party politicians, known for their anti-Berisha stance, formed a new party called Movement for Democracy.
- More than 4,000 soldiers of the U.N.-backed, 6,000-strong multinational force have already reached Albania.
ALBANIA
- The paper quotes prominent writer Ismail Kadare, now in France, as saying foreign media are to blame for the unrest in Albania.
- Editorial says Albanian ministers humiliate themselves by agreeing to meet all foreigners irrespective of their ranks.
- Socialist Party leader Fatos Nano failed to convince Europe that his party has been reformed and may be fit to rule Albania.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- Albanian-born Mother Teresa calls on all Albanians to drop their weapons and work for peace and stability.
- Luciano Forlani, commander of Italian-led multinational security mission, has ruled out direct contacts with rebel committees which control much of the south.
- Democratic Party is sure it will win the upcoming general elections.
ZERI I POPULLIT
- If Fino's government falls, Albania will be engulfed in civil war, Italian Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta is quoted as saying.
- Berisha and his Democratic Party are the main culprits to blame for the economic, financial and political disaster in Albania.
